title: Claim the hotel cost
recap: Pipo emailed Cloudhop Air to get your hotel night back.
funFact: Agents can keep your calendar up to date, too. Next, Pipo adds your new flight!
postcard: an airline email with a hotel receipt clipped to it, flying into an inbox, subject: {subject}
situation: Your refund claim is in. Should I email Cloudhop Air about the hotel you paid for that night?
facts: 🔖 Booking code QX7R4K, refund claim filed
🏨 Hotel that night: $85, back to your card
📎 You have the hotel receipt to attach
👀 You want to read it before it goes
systemPrompt: You are Pipo, a friendly personal assistant for a busy executive. You can send emails for them. You do what they ask: if they ask you to send something, you send it; if they ask to see it first, you write a draft and wait for their OK.

tools.name: send_email
tools.description: Send the email right away. Use this when the user wants it sent.

to.description: Who gets the email: a person, an email address or a mailing list

subject.description: The subject line, up to 8 words

body.description: The email text, up to 50 words

tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Write the email and show it to the user without sending it, so they can check it first. Use this when the user wants to read it before it goes out.

to.description: Who gets the email: a person, an email address or a mailing list

subject.description: The subject line, up to 8 words

body.description: The email text, up to 50 words

lines.text: Draft ready, waiting for your OK to send

slots.label: What do you want Pipo to do?

pieces.label: Email Cloudhop Air for the hotel cost
pieces.text: Email Cloudhop Air (refunds@cloudhop-air.com) to get back the hotel I had to pay for when they canceled my Friday flight.

pieces.label: Booking code and my refund claim
pieces.text: Mention my booking code QX7R4K and the refund claim I already filed for the ticket.

pieces.label: $85 back to my card
pieces.text: Ask for the $85 hotel night back to my card.

pieces.label: The hotel receipt is attached
pieces.text: Say the hotel receipt is attached.

pieces.label: Tell them they ruined my week!
pieces.text: Tell them they ruined my week!
pieces.tip: Venting feels good, but a calm email with the facts gets your money back faster.

pieces.label: Show me the email first
pieces.text: Show me the email before you send it.

flaws.hint: "The airline" doesn't say which one or where to write.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know the airline's address, so the email isn't going to Cloudhop Air.

flaws.hint: You didn't give Pipo your booking code.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't have your booking code, so the airline can't match the email to your claim.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo how much the hotel was, or where the money should go.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you want $85 back to your card, so the email doesn't say what to pay or where.

flaws.hint: You didn't tell Pipo the receipt is attached.
flaws.explain: Pipo didn't know you have the receipt, so the email doesn't mention it and the airline may ask for proof.

flaws.hint: When money is on the line, reading the email first is worth the extra second.
flaws.explain: Pipo sent it straight away, so you never checked what it asked for.

lesson: A claim email needs your booking code, the exact amount and the proof. Read it before it goes.
